Creating custom CGFs (from vectorized functions)

Source: vignettes/custom-cgf.Rmd
custom-cgf.Rmd

This vignette shows how to build a new CGF object when you can write down:

  • the CGF K(t;θ)K(t;\theta) and its derivatives (at least up to order 4), and
  • (optionally) the domain constraint(s) for tt.

The recommended constructor for most univariate or elementwise models is:

  • createCGF_fromVectorisedFunctions()

where you provide vectorized derivative functions that operate elementwise on tvec.

What you must provide

For createCGF_fromVectorisedFunctions(), you provide 5 vectorized functions:

  • K_vectorized_func(tvec, param) returning a numeric vector of length length(tvec)
  • K1_vectorized_func(tvec, param) returning a numeric vector
  • K2_vectorized_func(tvec, param) returning a numeric vector (diagonal of the Hessian)
  • K3_vectorized_func(tvec, param) returning a numeric vector
  • K4_vectorized_func(tvec, param) returning a numeric vector

The constructor then builds:

  • K(tvec,param) as sum(K_vectorized_func(...)),
  • K2(tvec,param) as a diagonal matrix with entries K2_vectorized_func(...),
  • and default higher-order operators needed for the correction term.

Often very useful:

  • ineq_constraint_func(tvec,param) returning a numeric vector of constraints g(t,θ)g(t,\theta) with feasibility defined by g≤0g \le 0,
  • analytic_tvec_hat_func(x,param) if you can solve K1(t̂;θ)=xK_1(\hat t;\theta)=x in closed form,
  • specialized K2_solve / logdetK2 for performance.

Example: a Normal CGF (SPA is exact)

Let X∼N(μ,σ2)X \sim \mathrm{N}(\mu,\sigma^2). The CGF is K(t;μ,σ2)=μt+12σ2t2, K(t;\mu,\sigma^2) = \mu t + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2 t^2, and the derivatives are K1(t)=μ+σ2t,K2(t)=σ2,K3(t)=0,K4(t)=0. K_1(t) = \mu + \sigma^2 t,\quad K_2(t) = \sigma^2,\quad K_3(t)=0,\quad K_4(t)=0.

Below we implement a Normal CGF parameterized by (μ,logσ2)(\mu, \log\sigma^2) to ensure positivity of σ2\sigma^2.


NormalLogSigma2CGF <- createCGF_fromVectorisedFunctions(
  K_vectorized_func = function(tvec, param) {
    mu <- param[1]
    s2 <- exp(param[2])
    mu * tvec + 0.5 * s2 * tvec * tvec
  },
  K1_vectorized_func = function(tvec, param) {
    mu <- param[1]
    s2 <- exp(param[2])
    mu + s2 * tvec
  },
  K2_vectorized_func = function(tvec, param) {
    s2 <- exp(param[2])
    rep(s2, length(tvec))
  },
  K3_vectorized_func = function(tvec, param) rep(0, length(tvec)) * param[1],
  K4_vectorized_func = function(tvec, param) rep(0, length(tvec)) * param[1],

  # Optional: analytic saddlepoint t-hat for K1(t)=x
  analytic_tvec_hat_func = function(x, param) {
    mu <- param[1]
    s2 <- exp(param[2])
    (x - mu) / s2
  },

  op_name = "NormalLogSigma2CGF"
)

# Simulate iid data
set.seed(1)
B <- 50
mu_true <- 1.5
s2_true <- 2.0
y <- rnorm(B, mean = mu_true, sd = sqrt(s2_true))

# iid CGF for (Y_1,...,Y_B)
cgB <- iidReplicatesCGF(NormalLogSigma2CGF, iidReps = B, block_size = 1)

# Saddlepoint MLE (should match exact normal MLE very closely; for Normal SPA is exact)
fit <- find.saddlepoint.MLE(
  observed.data  = y,
  cgf            = cgB,
  starting.theta = c(0.01, log(1.3)),
  method         = "two_step"
)

# Exact MLE under Normal(mu, sigma^2):
mu_hat_exact <- mean(y)
s2_hat_exact <- mean((y - mu_hat_exact)^2)

cbind(
  spa_mle   = fit$MLEs.theta,
  exact_mle = c(mu_hat_exact, log(s2_hat_exact)),
  true      = c(mu_true, log(s2_true))
)
#>        spa_mle exact_mle      true
#> [1,] 1.6420553 1.6420553 1.5000000
#> [2,] 0.3036414 0.3036414 0.6931472

Adding a domain constraint (when needed)

Some distributions have a restricted CGF domain in tt. If K(t;θ)K(t;\theta) is only defined when g(t,θ)≤0g(t,\theta)\le 0, implement:


ineq_constraint_func = function(tvec, param) {
  # return a numeric vector; feasible if all entries <= 0
}

Example: if a univariate CGF is defined for t<b(θ)t < b(\theta), you can return tvec - b(theta).
